9117.t: Of unknown origin. Perhaps related to ἀσκός (askós, “skin, hide”), thus with original meaning "to prepare a skin".

9100.t: From ἀρόω (ăróō, “I plow”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, masculine agent noun suffix). See also ἄροτρον (árotron).

9199.t: Unclear. Has been derived from ἄρκυς (ắrkŭs, “net”).

9111.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ér-ye-, a ye-present from the root *h₂erh₃- (“to plough”). Cognates include Old Armenian արաւր (arawr), Latin arō, Old Church Slavonic орати (orati), and Old English erian (Early Modern English ear).

9105.t: From ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “beginning”) + ἡγέομαι (hēgéomai, “to lead”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix).

9167.t: From the adjective ἁγνός (hagnós, “chaste”), unless this is a folk etymology which led to the cultural associations with chastity, rather than the reverse.

9121.t: From ἀστήρ (astḗr, “star”) + λέγω (légō, “to compute, to reckon”) + -ος (-os).

9198.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éristos (“fittest, most fitting, most suitable”), the superlative of *h₂er- (“to fit, be suitable”).

9162.t: From ἁ- (hă-, “one, same”) + -πλόος (-plóos, “-fold”). Compare διπλόος (dĭplóos, “double”), as well as Latin simplex.

9197.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin.

9166.t: From Proto-Indo-European *m̥ǵ-éh₂-m, accusative singular of *méǵh₂s (“great”, whence μέγας (mégăs)).

9196.t: The formation is similar to κέλαδος (kélados) and ὅμαδος (hómados). Perhaps onomatopoeic but compare ἄραβος (árabos).

9140.t: According to Beekes, the connection with ἀφιέναι (aphiénai, “flowers”) proposed by Theophrastus is unsustainable.

9119.t: Solmsen connected σπαλύσσεται (spalússetai, “to rip, agitate”) and σφαλάσσειν (sphalássein, “to cut, sting”), but this is semantically unconvincing. It is rather a Pre-Greek word in view of the suffix, typical of plant names.

9138.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin, in view of the suffix -βος.

9102.t: This verb is generally reconstructed as *ἀϝερτάω (*ăwertắō), from ἀείρω (ăeírō, “to bind; to hang”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wer- (“to raise; to bind”); however, the derivation is unusual.

9110.t: From ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “a beginning, origin”) + -θεν (-then, “a suffix added to nouns to form adverbs of place from which: from”)

9129.t: From ἄσχολος (ắskholos, “occupied, busy”) + -ία (-íā, abstract noun suffix).

9158.t: Denominal verb of ἁλιεύς (halieús, “fisher”); also analyzable as ἅλς (háls, “saltwater, seawater”) + -εύω (-eúō).
